messages:
Ethan: Following up from the PM: root cause is a TTL misalignment + session-cache sticky SNI entries on the edge appliances. When DNS TTL dropped during a route flip, some clients kept using stale IPs and the session cache presented SNI that no longer matched the new backend cert. Result: TLS rejects -> client retry -> cross-region fallback.
Leila: Any concrete numbers on impact?
Ethan: From the traces: ~2.6% of connections in the spike window saw TLS_REJECT + retry. Majority were short-lived API clients (2xx normal, but extra latency 400-800ms).
Marta: I've repro'd locally with a small harness. Steps: spin up two edge nodes, flip DNS, set dns_ttl=10s and cache_ttl=30s, then issue serialized connections. Paste of the harness config below:
```
# harness config (sanitized)
edgeA: ip=10.0.1.2 cert=sni-old
edgeB: ip=10.0.1.3 cert=sni-new
client: reuse_sessions=true
dns_ttl: 10
session_cache_ttl: 30
```
Marta: Repro is reliable when session_cache_ttl > dns_ttl and route flip occurs during active reuse window.
Leila: Good find. Short-term mitigation options?
Ethan: Proposals: 1) bump DNS TTL lower-bound for our dynamic flips (avoid very low TTLs during rollout windows), 2) add proactive SNI eviction on session cache when route map changes, 3) add an ecdsa/cert mismatch friendly fallback to attempt TLS renegotiation instead of immediate reject.
QA-runner: For immediate ops: can we implement an emergency config change to increase session_cache_ttl-to-dns_ttl parity? Might be safer to align rather than immediate evictions.
Marta: We should be careful: increasing session_cache_ttl means stale certs linger longer. I prefer eviction + graceful retry.
Ethan: OK compromise: short-term = disable aggressive dns_ttl=5s tests during rollouts and add a 2s "safety hold" window where we pause route flips when active session reuse > 100/s. Mid-term = SNI eviction + metric. Long-term = atomic route map swaps at edge with synchronized SNI map.
Leila: Can we get owners and dates so I can add to the postmortem action tracker?
Ethan: Owners and ETA: 
- Ethan: implement session-cache SNI eviction + unit tests (ETA: 2026-04-02 EOD)
- Marta: create reproducible harness + automated test to catch TTL/cache regressions (ETA: 2026-03-29)
- Leila: ops runbook updates + turn off low-dns-ttl experiments during rollouts (ETA: 2026-03-26 COB)
- QA-runner: add canary checks that monitor "tls_reject_retry_rate" and fail rollouts if > 5% for 5m (ETA: 2026-03-30)
- ops-bot: add automated annotation on route flips including current session reuse count (ETA: 2026-03-28)
Ethan: I'll open the PR for eviction and link the rollout plan. Note: rollout should include staged enable on one region and manual watch for tls_reject_retry_rate for 24h.
Marta: I'll add the harness to CI as a nightly job to catch regressions. Will also add a specific test that simulates dns flip + session reuse.
Leila: ops-bot, please schedule a follow-up sync next week to verify progress.
ops-bot: scheduled: "sni-ttl-followup" on 2026-03-31T15:00:00Z with attendees: Ethan, Leila, Marta, QA-runner. Reminder set.
QA-runner: quick note on customer impact comms: this explains transient latency spikes and rare retries; recommending a short blurb with root cause + actions and that no data loss occurred. I'll draft and send for approval.
Ethan: ack. Last thing: can folks react with :white_check_mark: when tasks are created so I can link them from the postmortem?
Leila: :white_check_mark:
Marta: :white_check_mark:
QA-runner: :white_check_mark:
Ethan: thanks. I'll update the PM with these action owners and timeline. If anyone notices similar TLS patterns tied to DNS experiments, please tag #incidents and @Ethan.
